stem: Which backup type backs up every selected file regardless of when it last changed, taking the longest but making restores simplest?
explanation: A full backup backs up every selected file regardless of when it last changed, taking the longest but making restores simplest.

distractorExplanations.b: Incremental backups instead: backs up only files that changed since the last backup of any type, keeping backups small but requiring the full chain to restore.
distractorExplanations.c: Differential backups instead: backs up all files that changed since the last full backup, growing larger each day but needing only two backups to restore.
distractorExplanations.d: A snapshot captures point-in-time system state (often at the storage/VM layer) rather than following a scheduled full/incremental/differential file backup cycle.

distractorExplanations.d: Non-repudiation ensures an action can't be denied after the fact — it's related but not one of the three CIA triad elements.

distractorExplanations.b: Authentication instead: verifies that a user is who they claim to be, typically with a password, token, or biometric.
distractorExplanations.c: Authorization instead: determines what an already-verified user is allowed to do.
distractorExplanations.d: Encryption protects data confidentiality — it isn't one of the three AAA components.

stem: Which type of firewall inspects each packet's header (source/destination IP and port) in isolation against a rule set, with no awareness of connection state?
explanation: A packet-filtering firewall is defined by this behaviour.

distractorExplanations.b: Stateful firewall instead tracks the state of active connections and only allows traffic that matches an established or expected session.
distractorExplanations.c: Application-layer (proxy) firewall instead inspects traffic up to Layer 7, understanding the specific application protocol it's filtering.
distractorExplanations.d: Next-generation firewall (NGFW) instead combines stateful inspection with deep packet inspection, intrusion prevention, and application awareness in one device.

stem: A newly connected switch port shows extremely high late collisions and the link light flickers, even though traffic volume is low. The port is configured for 100 Mbps/full-duplex; the attached NIC is set to auto-negotiate. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: A duplex mismatch — the NIC auto-negotiated half-duplex against the switch's forced full-duplex
A bad DNS server configuration on the host
The switch port is assigned to the wrong VLAN
An expired DHCP lease on the host

explanation: Forcing one side of a link to full-duplex while the other auto-negotiates commonly results in a duplex mismatch (the auto side falls back to half-duplex), which produces exactly this symptom: late collisions and degraded performance despite a low-traffic, seemingly fine link.

distractorExplanations.b: A DNS misconfiguration would cause name resolution failures, not collisions at the physical/data-link layer.
distractorExplanations.c: A DHCP lease issue would show up as an addressing problem (e.g., an APIPA address), not collisions.
distractorExplanations.d: A wrong VLAN would cause connectivity/isolation issues, not late collisions.

stem: A user reports their laptop has an IP address of 169.254.34.12 and cannot reach anything on the network. What does this address indicate?

options.text: The laptop is correctly configured with a static private IP address
The laptop received a valid address from a DHCP scope reserved for guests
The laptop couldn't reach a DHCP server and self-assigned an APIPA address
The laptop is using a public IP address assigned by the ISP

explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is the APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing) range. A Windows host assigns itself an address from this range when it can't contact a DHCP server, which is a strong sign of a DHCP or connectivity problem upstream.

distractorExplanations.b: 169.254.x.x is never used as an intentional static assignment on a working network — it's a self-assigned fallback.
distractorExplanations.c: DHCP scopes are never configured in the 169.254.0.0/16 range; that block is reserved for APIPA.
distractorExplanations.d: 169.254.0.0/16 is a link-local range, not a publicly routable ISP-assigned range.
